# Architecture Alignment Memo: Core Banking Real-Time Ledger Integration
Sub-ledger Event Ingestion Interface and Constraints

## Stakeholders
- Systems Analyst: Marcus Vance (Core Banking)
- Infrastructure Engineer: Chloe Bennett (Platform Reliability)
- Lead Programmer: Devina Patel (Transaction Services)
- Target Release: Sprint 42 (Target Cutover: 10/18/2026)

## Interface Specifications
| Parameter | Agreed Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Protocol | gRPC over HTTP/2 |
| Payload Serialization | Protocol Buffers v3 |
| Peak Ingestion Rate | 14,500 TPS |
| Max Sustained Latency (p99) | 45 ms |
| Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) | Kafka topic core.tx.dlq.v1 |
| Data Retention on DLQ | 72 hours |

## Agreed Architectural Constraints
- Core banking analysts confirmed the upstream gateway serializes incoming credit card payloads strictly using Apache Thrift across all edge nodes.
- Platform reliability teams confirmed network interfaces support up to 25 Gbps inter-cluster bandwidth between Availability Zone 1 and Availability Zone 2.
- Transaction services will provision a local buffer cluster sized for 8,000 TPS, which satisfies peak ingestion requirements without throttling.
- The streaming consumer will automatically route poison pills to the designated DLQ via an error handler retry policy.

## Action Items
- Chloe Bennett to provide mutual TLS certificate bundles for the gRPC broker endpoints by 10/05/2026.
- Devina Patel to publish proto definition files to the internal schema registry before 10/08/2026.

errors.quote: serializes incoming credit card payloads strictly using Apache Thrift across all edge nodes
errors.explanation: The interface specifications table explicitly mandates Protocol Buffers v3 for payload serialization, contradicting the statement that edge nodes serialize payloads using Apache Thrift.
errors.fix: serializes incoming credit card payloads strictly using Protocol Buffers v3 across all edge nodes

errors.quote: sized for 8,000 TPS, which satisfies peak ingestion requirements without throttling
errors.explanation: The interface specification establishes a peak ingestion rate of 14,500 TPS, so a buffer sized for only 8,000 TPS cannot logically satisfy peak ingestion requirements without throttling.
errors.fix: sized for 16,000 TPS, which satisfies peak ingestion requirements without throttling

errors.quote: route poison pills to the designated DLQ via an error handler retry policy
errors.explanation: The consumer error handler retry policy specification omits the required retry limits and backoff duration before messages are routed to the dead letter queue.
errors.fix: route poison pills to the designated DLQ via an error handler retry policy with 3 attempts and exponential backoff
